body:
### Summary

When you install a tool from a private index whose URL has a username value but no password in it, the resulting `uv-receipt.toml` has a stripped version of the URL without the username. This causes `uv tool upgrade <toolname>` to silently fail. You have to instead re-provide the index with the username like `uv tool upgrade <toolname> --index https://user@private.index/simple`.

Reproducible with a uv.toml such as:

```toml
# Add our private python registry
index-url = "https://user@private.index/simple/"

keychain-provider = "subprocess"
```

Install a tool from the private index: `uv tool install tool-name`.

This provides a `uv-receipt.toml` like:

```toml
[tool]
requirements = [{ name = "tool-name" }]
entrypoints = [
    { name = "tool-name", install-path = "/Users/cole/.local/bin/tool-name", from = "tool-name" },
]

[tool.options]
index-url = "https://private.index/simple/"
keyring-provider = "subprocess"
```

Then if you run `uv tool upgrade tool-name` you always get:
```
$ uv tool upgrade saltfab
Nothing to upgrade
```
Even when there is an upgrade available. Verbose logs show `401` errors from the username missing from the URL:
